title: Febrile Illness & Sepsis Screening
description: Evaluation of fever and inflammatory signs with explicit screening for sepsis, meningitis, and shock.

risk_rules.name: Suspected Sepsis / Meningococcal Purpura Emergency
risk_rules.reason: Fever associated with a non-blanching dark purple/red petechial rash, acute disorientation/confusion, or lethargy. Consistent with fulminant sepsis or meningococcemia.

risk_rules.name: Fever with Nuchal Rigidity (Meningitis Pattern)
risk_rules.reason: High fever combined with severe neck stiffness and photophobia, indicating meningeal irritation.

risk_rules.name: Prolonged High Fever or High-Risk Host
risk_rules.reason: Temperature exceeding 39.5°C (103°F) or fever persisting beyond 5 days with marked prostration or in an immunocompromised individual.

risk_rules.name: Febrile Syndrome with Focal Organ Symptoms
risk_rules.reason: Fever presenting with localized symptoms such as burning urination (dysuria), unilateral earache, or sinus pain requiring clinical assessment.
risk_rules.possible_concern: Focal bacterial infection (e.g. Pyelonephritis, Sinusitis, Otitis)

risk_rules.name: Short-Duration Low-Grade Febrile Viral Illness
risk_rules.reason: Low-grade temperature (<38.5°C) lasting less than 48 hours, clear sensorium, good fluid intake, and mild upper respiratory symptoms.

possible_conditions.name: Severe systemic infection / Sepsis
possible_conditions.reason_template: High fever accompanied by confusion, purpuric spots, rapid breathing, or poor perfusion.
possible_conditions.caveat: Decision support alert. Immediate emergency department evaluation and blood cultures/antibiotics are vital.

possible_conditions.name: Acute bacterial infection
possible_conditions.reason_template: Persistent elevated temperature with localized focal symptoms (urinary, pulmonary, or ENT).
possible_conditions.caveat: Clinical examination and targeted lab testing needed to determine if antimicrobial therapy is indicated.

possible_conditions.name: Self-limiting viral syndrome
possible_conditions.reason_template: Mild fever with diffuse myalgias, coryza, and preserved general clinical status.
possible_conditions.caveat: Supportive hydration and rest advised; seek review if fever persists > 3 days or red flags emerge.

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Direct screening for life-threatening sepsis and purpura fulminans.
recommended_questions.question: Do you have any new dark red or purple spots on your skin that do not fade when pressed, or any confusion?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Screens for acute bacterial or viral meningitis.
recommended_questions.question: Does your neck feel unusually stiff, or does it hurt when you try to tuck your chin to your chest?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Measures physiological severity and chronological trajectory.
recommended_questions.question: What was the highest temperature measured, and how many days has the fever been present?

recommended_questions.safety_relevance: Isolates the anatomical source of infection.
recommended_questions.question: Are you experiencing pain when urinating, severe back pain, or a productive cough?
